summary: Independently verified T85's closure of T84#F-001 (unmemoised destination read, a second quadratic) and T84#F-003 (escape-blind description bracket pairing). Built my own pre-T85 reconstruction from the shipped file (not reused from any prior round) by reverting exactly the two documented mechanisms, and reproduced both defects on it independently before confirming both are closed on shipped code, at the detector and all four public boundaries, pinned by regressions. Ran T84-bypass.ts, T84-escape.ts, T84b-destfail-check.ts, T84b-destfail-4boundary.ts and T85-parity.ts myself (the last against the real reconstruction, not a shim, reproducing T85's own 28000-document run byte-for-byte: spanMoveCount 0, hostReleaseCount 0). Wrote a new probe of my own (T88-neveroffset.ts) with three shapes that never repeat a destination offset, attacking the disjointness argument directly rather than trusting the cache; all stay linear-or-sub-linear to 1MB. Independently re-ran the full T85-cost.ts boundary sweep to completion (T84 had abandoned it as impractical pre-fix): boundariesOverOneSecond: [], worst shape escapedCloseRunWithDef at 660.3ms. Confirmed 18/19 prior matrices byte-identical, benign corpus unchanged (16 files/62 findings/7 Part-B ids), and the accepted container-block limitation (T84#F-002) unchanged at exactly 17 bypassing rows. Ratified the 'flag but never skip' cursor-guard rule as the correct permanent shape. No blocking findings; two documentation-grade info findings recorded (absence of a length gate at the boundary layer as defense-in-depth, and a one-count corpus-scan drift traced to this review's own gdctx tooling artifacts).
